name: Stress
supportType: School counselor, peer support group, or stress-management resources (relaxation tips, time-management help)
seekProfessionalWhen: Stress keeps affecting your sleep, school or work, relationships, or daily routine—and self-care ideas do not seem to help after a while.
gentleSuggestion: Try a short break: stretch, drink water, or take a few slow breaths. Write down one small next step so tasks feel less overwhelming.

name: Sleep-related concern
supportType: Sleep hygiene guides, school nurse or wellness office, or a brief check-in with a counselor about sleep habits
seekProfessionalWhen: Sleep problems last several weeks, you feel exhausted most days, or poor sleep makes school, work, or mood much harder to manage.
gentleSuggestion: Try a calm wind-down (dim lights, no screens for 30 minutes, same bedtime). Small routine changes can help over time.

name: Low mood
relatesTo: Feeling sad, empty, or down for a while
Loneliness or pulling away from others
Low motivation or loss of interest in usual activities
supportType: Talking with someone you trust, peer support, or a school counselor for general emotional support
seekProfessionalWhen: Low mood lasts more than about two weeks, you often feel hopeless, or you stop enjoying things that used to matter to you.
gentleSuggestion: Send a short message to someone you trust. A small walk outside or one activity you used to enjoy may help a little.

name: Anxiety/Panic
relatesTo: Physical signs of anxiety (tight chest, restlessness)
Panic-like episodes or feeling constantly on edge
supportType: Grounding and breathing exercises, school counselor, or mental health counseling for coping skills
seekProfessionalWhen: Worry or panic happens often, feels very intense, or gets in the way of school, sleep, friendships, or leaving home.
gentleSuggestion: Ground yourself: name 5 things you see, 4 you feel, 3 you hear. Slow breathing (inhale 4 counts, exhale 6) can ease body tension.

name: General concern
relatesTo: Not sure which label fits—but something feels off
supportType: Trusted adult (family, teacher, mentor), general wellness resources, or a counselor for an open conversation
seekProfessionalWhen: Feelings stay with you, grow stronger, or feel too heavy to handle alone—even if you are not sure what to call them.
gentleSuggestion: Your feelings are valid. Journaling for a few minutes may help you notice patterns. Talking with someone you trust is a good next step.
